elements.content: Communication Goal: I can greet people, introduce myself and others, spell my details, talk about jobs, and use survival phrases.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 1. First Contact
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: First Contact
- Materials: World map, city and job badges, contact cards, workshop registration script.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• introduce myself and another person
• spell names, emails, and phone numbers
• talk about jobs and ask for clarification
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: First lesson of the inspired track. Activate any greetings and personal details learners already know.

Next lesson: Lesson 2 recycles introductions and adds objects, rooms, and requests.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

hello — a greeting when you meet someone. Example: Hello, my name is Alex.
hi — an informal greeting. Example: Hi, how are you?
name — the word people use to call you. Example: My name is Sara.
spell — to say the letters of a word. Example: Can you spell your name, please?
email — a message sent by computer. Example: I send an email every morning.
phone — a mobile or telephone. Example: My phone is in my bag.
number — a symbol or amount. Example: What is your phone number?
job — the work a person does. Example: What is your job?
student — a person who studies. Example: I am a student.
teacher — a person who helps students learn. Example: She is my English teacher.
designer — a person who designs things. Example: She is a UX designer.
engineer — a person who designs or builds things. Example: He is an engineer.
nurse — a person who cares for sick people. Example: The nurse works in a hospital.
office — a place where people work. Example: I work in an office.
remote — working away from an office. Example: She works remote three days a week.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Hi, I'm ... I'm from ... (introducing yourself)
• This is ... She's / He's from ... (introducing another person)
• Can you spell that, please? (asking for spelling)
• My email is ... at ... dot com. (sharing an email address)
• What do you do? — I'm a designer. (asking and answering about jobs)
• Are you a student? — No, I'm a freelancer. (asking about work)
• Sorry, can you repeat that? (survival phrase)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a greeting when you meet someone'?
Which word means 'an informal greeting'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus: Alphabet vowel groups and polite question intonation

name /neɪm/ — long /eɪ/
email /ˈiːmeɪl/ — stress the first syllable
designer /dɪˈzaɪnə/ — stress the second syllable
repeat /rɪˈpiːt/ — stress the second syllable
Listen and repeat:
Hi, I'm Alex. I'm from Toronto. This is Maria. She's a designer. Sorry, can you repeat that?

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be' to say who someone is, how they feel, and where they are from.

Form:
The verb 'to be': I am / You are / He, she, it is / We are / They are. Negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he...?

Examples:
• I am a student.
• She is from Spain.
• We are happy today.
• They are not teachers.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My name ___ Alex.
They ___ from Italy.
I ___ tired today.
She ___ not a teacher.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am ... (a student / happy / from Egypt).
• She is ... (a teacher / tired / from Spain).
• They are ... (students / at home / happy).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
• Is she from France? — Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
• Are they happy? — Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write two true sentences with 'I am...' and 'I am not...'.
• Introduce two people in the class with 'He/She is...'.
Reading: First Contact

Welcome to HubSpace! Nadia is from Lyon. She is a UX designer. Kenji is from Osaka. He is a software engineer and he works remote. Camille and Leo are from Montreal. Camille is a freelance photographer, and Leo is a marketing manager. Their desk is next to the window. Are you a new member? What do you do?
What is Nadia's job?
Where is Kenji from?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Good morning! I'm calling about the workshop.
B: Great. What's your name?
A: Tomas Keller.
B: How do you spell that?
A: K-E-L-L-E-R.
B: And your email?
A: t dot keller at studio hyphen mail dot com.
B: Sorry, can you repeat that?
A: t dot keller at studio hyphen mail dot com.
How does Tomas spell his last name?
What is his email?
Speaking task: Speed-mingle: introduce yourself and one other person. Spell one detail and ask for a repeat.

• What do you say when you meet someone new?
• How do you spell your name?
• What do you do?
• Do you work remote or in an office?
• Which survival phrase do you need most?
Role-play: You are at a coworking welcome event. Introduce yourself, introduce a colleague, spell an email, and ask the host to repeat one detail.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a four-line contact card: name and city, job, email and phone, one survival phrase.
Model: Hi, I'm ... I'm a ... My email is ... at ... dot com. Sorry, can you repeat that?
